items.title: Degree-six cubic trace polynomial for a chiral representation
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement:
Let $H=SU(3)\times U(1)$, where $SU(3)=\{g\in M_3(\mathbb C):g^\dagger g=I_3,\det g=1\}$ and $U(1)=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$. For a finite-dimensional unitary representation $\rho:H\to U(V_\rho)$, let $A_\rho$ be a smooth anti-Hermitian matrix-valued one-form on a smooth manifold $X$, representing a connection in a local trivialization, and set $F_\rho=dA_\rho+A_\rho\wedge A_\rho$. Define the degree-six invariant polynomial

$$\mathcal I_6(\rho,A_\rho):=2\pi\left[\operatorname{tr}_{V_\rho}\exp\!\left(-\frac{iF_\rho}{2\pi}\right)\right]_6=\frac{i}{24\pi^2}\operatorname{tr}_{V_\rho}(F_\rho\wedge F_\rho\wedge F_\rho),$$

where the exponential is its formal power series and $[\,\cdot\,]_6$ selects the differential-form component of degree six. This is a homogeneous polynomial in the formal curvature; on a four-dimensional physical spacetime it is interpreted on the formal six-dimensional extension used for descent, not integrated as a six-form over spacetime. The normalization fixes anti-Hermitian generators, the fundamental trace, and the overall coefficient once and for all.

For the defining representation $E=\mathbb C^3$ with $\rho_E(g,z)=zg$, a background connection is $A_E=A+iB I_3$, where $A$ is an $\mathfrak{su}(3)$-valued one-form and $B$ is a real $U(1)$ connection one-form. The dual representation is $E^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(E,\mathbb C)$ with $\rho_{E^*}(g,z)=\rho_E(g,z)^{-T}$; its induced connection and curvature are $A_{E^*}=-A_E^T$ and $F_{E^*}=-F_E^T$.

items.title: A conjugate representation reverses the cubic anomaly polynomial
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement:
Let $H=SU(3)\times U(1)$, let $E=\mathbb C^3$ have representation $\rho_E(g,z)=zg$, and let $E^*$ be its dual representation. For a smooth background connection $A_E$ on a smooth manifold $X$, use the induced dual connection $A_{E^*}=-A_E^T$ and curvatures $F_E=dA_E+A_E\wedge A_E$ and $F_{E^*}=dA_{E^*}+A_{E^*}\wedge A_{E^*}$. With the degree-six polynomial $\mathcal I_6$ defined above, one has

$$\mathcal I_6(E^*,A_{E^*})=-\mathcal I_6(E,A_E).$$

For the canonical Chern–Simons transgression

$$Q_5(E,A_E):=3\frac{i}{24\pi^2}\int_0^1\operatorname{tr}_E\!\left(A_E\wedge F_{E,t}\wedge F_{E,t}\right)\,dt,\qquad F_{E,t}:=t\,dA_E+t^2A_E\wedge A_E,$$

the dual transgression satisfies $Q_5(E^*,A_{E^*})=-Q_5(E,A_E)$. Thus any common linear descent of this conjugate pair has zero total cubic polynomial and zero total first consistent descent representative.

items.title: A local counterterm changes only the representative of a local anomaly class
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement: Let $\mathcal A_U^{g,p}$ be the finite-jet horizontal-form spaces on a smooth open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, with nilpotent BRST differential $s$, horizontal differential $d_H$, and $sd_H+d_Hs=0$. In bidegree $(1,4)$, define $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$ as the ghost-number-one four-forms $a_4$ satisfying $sa_4+d_Hb_3=0$ for some $b_3$, modulo the subspace $\{sC_4+d_Hr_3:C_4\in\mathcal A_U^{0,4},\ r_3\in\mathcal A_U^{1,3}\}$. If a local counterterm changes an anomaly representative from $a_4$ to $a'_4=a_4+sC_4+d_Hr_3$, then $[a'_4]=[a_4]$ in $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$.

items.title: Local perturbative ’t Hooft anomaly modulo counterterms
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement:
Fix a four-dimensional smooth spacetime region $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with a stated orientation, spin structure, boundary conditions, and unit system. A selected model specifies a continuous global symmetry group $H$, its action on the fields and observables, the nondynamical background connections, the field and jet domains, a regulator and measure or formal perturbative generating functional, and the admissible local counterterms. A background connection is nondynamical model data: it transforms under local changes of background trivialization but is not integrated over.

Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{g,p}$ be the finite-jet horizontal $p$-forms of ghost number $g$ generated by the nondynamical background connections and their BRST ghost jets, without matter-field jets. Fix their coefficient field $\mathbb K$ as part of the model and restrict its nilpotent BRST differential $s$ and horizontal exterior derivative $d_H$ to this background subalgebra, with $s^2=d_H^2=sd_H+d_Hs=0$. The model supplies two $\mathbb K$-linear subspaces

$$\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{0,4},\qquad\mathcal N\subseteq\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{1,3}.$$

Here $\mathcal C$ is exactly the space of admissible changes of local background counterterm density, with coefficients and units giving dimensionless integrated action changes. The space $\mathcal N$ is exactly the space of boundary primitives whose $d_H$-derivatives are discarded in the infinitesimal variation under the stated support or boundary conditions. This convention must hold on every admitted background and ghost input; a surface contribution that is not discarded is not an element of $d_H\mathcal N$. Linearity of these two spaces is explicit model input, not a consequence of locality or nilpotence. No linear span of a restricted admissibility set is taken implicitly. If quantization or other restrictions instead make the admissible changes nonlinear, this vector-space quotient does not apply to them without a separately specified equivalence structure.

The space of compatible Wess–Zumino cocycles and the space of admissible changes are

$$Z^{1,4}:=\{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{1,4}:sa+d_Hb=0\text{ for some }b\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{2,3}\},\qquad B_{\mathcal C,\mathcal N}:=s\mathcal C+d_H\mathcal N.$$

Both are linear spaces, and $B_{\mathcal C,\mathcal N}\subseteq Z^{1,4}$: for $a=sc+d_Hn$ choose the ghost-number-two three-form $b=sn$, giving $sa+d_Hb=s^2c+sd_Hn+d_Hsn=0$. More generally, if $sa+d_Hb=0$, then $a'=a+sc+d_Hn$ obeys $sa'+d_H(b+sn)=0$, so every admitted representative change preserves consistency. The witness space for $b$ has bidegree $(2,3)$ and is distinct from the boundary-ambiguity space $\mathcal N$ of bidegree $(1,3)$.

An infinitesimal local anomaly representative is a specified $a_4\in Z^{1,4}$ for the model's quantum background variation. The **local perturbative ’t Hooft anomaly** is its class in

$$H^{1,4}_{\mathcal C,\mathcal N}(s\mid d_H):=Z^{1,4}/B_{\mathcal C,\mathcal N},\qquad a'_4\sim a_4\ \Longleftrightarrow\ a'_4-a_4=sc+d_Hn\text{ for some }c\in\mathcal C,\ n\in\mathcal N.$$

The subspace property makes this an equivalence relation and a quotient vector space. Its class is zero exactly when $a_4=sc+d_Hn$ for some such $c,n$; adding the admissible counterterm density $-c$ then leaves only the discarded term $d_Hn$. Conversely, if adding an admissible density $c'$ leaves a discarded term, $a_4+sc'=d_Hn$, then $a_4=s(-c')+d_Hn$ has zero class. This is precisely cancellation of the infinitesimal local background variation in the declared convention. The ordinary unrestricted relative cohomology $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$ is the special case $\mathcal C=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{0,4}$ and $\mathcal N=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{1,3}$ with a boundary convention discarding all these total derivatives; it is not substituted for a restricted model quotient.

Any prescribed noninvariance of the classical action or selected couplings is an explicit-symmetry-breaking insertion and is separated before assigning this quantum anomaly class. It is not, by itself, a measure anomaly. A claim of anomaly matching therefore assumes the stated classical symmetry, or carries such breaking insertions separately.

This definition applies to a global symmetry whose background is nondynamical. If the same local class concerns a field integrated over as a gauge redundancy, it is a local gauge anomaly, not a ’t Hooft anomaly; an uncancelled gauge anomaly obstructs the proposed gauging unless a separately specified cancellation mechanism is included. The definition addresses only infinitesimal transformations and makes no claim about large or disconnected transformations, determinant-line holonomy, torsion phases, or a physical continuum limit.

items.title: Flat-space chiral anomaly-matching data and regulator convention
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and flat oriented Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-,+,+,+)$ and its standard spin structure. Fix Dirac matrices by $\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}I$ and $\gamma_5=i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3=-i\gamma_0\gamma_1\gamma_2\gamma_3$; set $P_+=(I+\gamma_5)/2$ and $P_-=I-P_+$. Here $\gamma_0=-\gamma^0$ and $\gamma_j=\gamma^j$ for spatial $j$; this is Bilal's mostly-plus positive-chirality convention, Eq. (2.20), used by the adopted source-normalized determinant law below. Reversing this chirality convention would reverse the one-species anomaly sign. The global symmetry group is the fixed global form $H=SU(3)\times U(1)_V$, acting on a finite multiset $S$ of massless positive-chirality Weyl fields. Each field is a Grassmann-odd smooth compactly supported section of $\operatorname{im}(P_+)\otimes V_i$, where $V_i$ carries a specified finite-dimensional unitary representation $R_i$ of $H$. The chiral kinetic operator is $\mathcal D_{+,i}=P_-i\gamma^\mu D_{\mu,i}P_+$ from positive to negative chirality; its regulated determinant phase is a formal perturbative input. The matter field has mass dimension $3/2$; the background potentials have mass dimension one, their curvature two-forms dimension two, and all $U(1)_V$ charges and trace coefficients are dimensionless. The backgrounds are global one-forms on the trivial bundles over $M$, vary smoothly, and have compact support; the global symmetry is not integrated over as a dynamical gauge redundancy.

For each species, the background covariant derivative is $D_{\mu,i}=\partial_\mu+\rho_{i*}(A_\mu,iB_\mu)$ in its representation, where $A$ is an anti-Hermitian $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ connection, $B$ is a real $U(1)_V$ connection, and $\rho_{i*}:\mathfrak{su}(3)\oplus i\mathbb R\to\mathfrak u(V_i)$ is the derived Lie-algebra representation. Set $F_A=dA+A\wedge A$ and $f=dB$, and write $A_i:=\rho_{i*}(A,iB)$ and $F_i:=dA_i+A_i\wedge A_i$; thus $D_{\mu,i}=\partial_\mu+(A_i)_\mu$. For $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$, $A_E=A+iB I_3$ and $F_E=F_A+ifI_3$; for $E^*=(\bar{\mathbf3},-1)$, $A_{E^*}=-A^T-iB I_3$ and $F_{E^*}=-F_A^T-ifI_3$. Local transformations are $A\mapsto g^{-1}Ag+g^{-1}dg$ and $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$ for compactly supported $g: M\to SU(3)$ and $\alpha:M\to\mathbb R$; the $U(1)$ group element is $e^{i\alpha}$. Let $c$ be the ghost-number-one odd $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ ghost and $\eta$ the ghost-number-one odd real $U(1)_V$ ghost. The finite-jet BRST differential for $\mathfrak h=\mathfrak{su}(3)\oplus i\mathbb R$ is specified on components by $sA_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$, $sc=-[c,c]/2$, $sB_\mu=\partial_\mu\eta$, $s\eta=0$, and $s\psi_i=-\rho_{i*}(c,i\eta)\psi_i$; it acts on jets by commuting with total derivatives. The $U(1)_V$ factor is central. On horizontal forms use the supplier's extension $s(dx^\mu\wedge a)=-dx^\mu\wedge s(a)$, so $sd_H+d_Hs=0$. In particular the whole one-form obeys $sB=-d_H\eta$; the positive component rule is not a whole-form equation.

For an ordinary compactly supported infinitesimal parameter $\epsilon=\epsilon^aT_a:M\to\mathfrak{su}(3)$ and $\alpha:M\to\mathbb R$, define a linear map $\mathcal E^p_{\epsilon,\alpha}$ from ghost-number-one background horizontal $p$-forms to ordinary $p$-forms. In the unique normal form with all $dx$ factors to the left and the single ghost jet to the right, replace $c_I^a$ by $\partial_I\epsilon^a$ and $\eta_I$ by $\partial_I\alpha$, leaving background jets unchanged. Every such form has precisely one ghost factor because the background algebra has no negative-ghost generators. This is a linear map on that homogeneous component, not an algebra homomorphism on the exterior ghost algebra. It commutes with $d_H$. If $C_p$ is ghost-free, the finite-jet chain rule gives $\mathcal E^p_{\epsilon,\alpha}(sC_p)=(-1)^p\delta_{\epsilon,\alpha}C_p$: the sign moves $s$ past the $p$ coordinate one-forms, and the component rules give the ordinary infinitesimal field variation. Thus in physical degree four $\mathcal E^4(sC_4)=\delta C_4$, and $d_H$-exact terms evaluate to ordinary total derivatives. The degree-five descent is first formed on the formal auxiliary extension used for the degree-six polynomial, before restriction to $M$; there $\mathcal E^5(sI_5)=-\delta I_5$. Consequently $sI_5+d_HI_4^{(1)}=0$ yields the physical convention $\delta I_5=d_H\mathcal E^4(I_4^{(1)})$.

The anomaly-matching data include one common Pauli–Villars subtraction prescription for the chiral triangle graphs, with opposite-statistics regulator fields and regulator masses taken to the large-mass limit, together with the consistent effective-action variation convention and compact-support boundary conditions. The local anomaly complex is the finite-jet background subalgebra generated by $A,B$ and their BRST ghosts, with no matter-field jets, so its ghost-number-zero four-forms are precisely the admitted local counterterms. In the notation of the local-anomaly definition, fix the full linear spaces $\mathcal C=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},M}^{0,4}$ and $\mathcal N=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},M}^{1,3}$ over the same coefficient field as this background algebra. Evaluation uses compactly supported backgrounds and ghost parameters, so every ghost-number-one boundary primitive and its derivatives have compact support and the integral of its total derivative vanishes. Thus this selected scheme uses the full relative quotient $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)=H^{1,4}_{\mathcal C,\mathcal N}(s\mid d_H)$; no background-gauge-invariance condition is imposed on an individual counterterm. In particular, for real dimensionless $\lambda$, the four-form $C_4=\lambda B\wedge K_3(A)$ is admitted, where $K_3(A):=\operatorname{tr}(A\wedge dA+\tfrac23A\wedge A\wedge A)$. As an explicit source-backed one-loop input, after the regulator masses are taken to infinity this selected prescription assigns to each positive-chirality species $R_i$ the consistent local anomaly obtained by descent from $\mathcal I_6(R_i,A_i)$ of the preceding cubic-polynomial definition. The fixed linear descent map is normalized by $\mathcal I_6=dI^{(0)}_5$, $sI^{(0)}_5+d_HI^{(1)}_4=0$, and $sI^{(1)}_4+d_HI^{(2)}_3=0$, with $\delta_{\epsilon,\alpha}\Gamma=\sum_{i\in S}\int_M\mathcal E^4_{\epsilon,\alpha}(I^{(1)}_4(R_i,A_i))$. This determinant law is an adopted regulator input in the data, not a locally derived theorem about every regulator. The total polynomial is $\mathcal I_6^{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_{i\in S}\mathcal I_6(R_i,A_i)$, and its local anomaly class is interpreted using the preceding local ’t Hooft-anomaly definition. No large-transformation test, torsion calculation, mixed gravitational term, dynamical gauge quantization, or continuum-existence result is included.

items.title: Local anomaly cancellation for a conjugate chiral pair
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement:
Use the selected flat-space anomaly-matching model on oriented $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-,+,+,+)$ and natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Its nondynamical global-symmetry backgrounds are a smooth compactly supported anti-Hermitian $SU(3)$ connection $A$ and a smooth compactly supported real $U(1)_V$ connection $B$ on the trivial bundles. The finite field spectrum consists of two massless positive-chirality Weyl species, one in $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$ and one in its dual $E^*=(\bar{\mathbf3},-1)$. The background is not integrated over. Use one common large-mass Pauli–Villars subtraction scheme and the consistent effective-action convention fixed in the model data.

Adopt the source-backed one-loop input that each positive-chirality species in this regulator has consistent local variation given by descent from $\mathcal I_6(R)=2\pi[\operatorname{tr}_R\exp(-iF_R/(2\pi))]_6$, with the same linear descent for every species: $\mathcal I_6=dI_5^{(0)}$, $sI_5^{(0)}+d_HI_4^{(1)}=0$, and $sI_4^{(1)}+d_HI_3^{(2)}=0$, and $\delta_{\epsilon,\alpha}\Gamma=\sum_R\int_M\mathcal E^4_{\epsilon,\alpha}(I_4^{(1)}(R))$. Here $s$ is the component BRST differential extended with $s(dx^\mu\wedge a)=-dx^\mu\wedge s(a)$. The linear map $\mathcal E^4_{\epsilon,\alpha}$ writes each ghost-number-one form with its four $dx$ factors on the left, then replaces its single $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ or real $U(1)_V$ ghost jet by the corresponding ordinary parameter jet; it is not an algebra substitution on products of ghosts. The local anomaly class is the class of $I_4^{(1)}$ in $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$: local ghost-number-one four-forms satisfying the second descent equation, modulo $s$-variations of admitted local counterterms and total derivatives.

Then the total perturbative local anomaly class of this conjugate pair vanishes. This conclusion concerns only the identity component of the background-transformation group in the adopted one-loop convention; it asserts no absence of large-transformation or torsion anomalies and no consistency result for a dynamical gauge redundancy.

title: Perturbative ’t Hooft Anomalies and Counterterms — Examples

items.title: A single chiral fundamental has a nonzero local polynomial
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement:
Use the same flat-space background convention but take the spectrum to contain only one positive-chirality species $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$. Its polynomial is

$$\mathcal I_6(E)=\frac{i}{24\pi^2}\left(\operatorname{tr}F_A^3+3i f\wedge\operatorname{tr}F_A^2+3(if)^3\right),$$

where $F_A$ is the anti-Hermitian $SU(3)$ curvature, $f=dB$ is the $U(1)_V$ curvature, and the expression is evaluated as a degree-six polynomial on the formal extension used for descent. The mixed $U(1)_V$–$SU(3)^2$ term and the pure $U(1)_V^3$ term have nonzero coefficients. This example verifies that the one-field polynomial is not the zero invariant polynomial; it does not claim that the associated relative BRST class is nontrivial modulo every admissible counterterm or that a global anomaly has been evaluated.

items.title: A mixed-background counterterm shifts the local representative
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a smooth compactly supported anti-Hermitian $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ connection one-form on trivial $\mathbb R^{1,3}$, with curvature $F_A=dA+A\wedge A$, and let $B$ be a smooth real $U(1)_V$ background one-form with compactly supported gauge parameter $\alpha$. In natural units, $[A]=[B]=\text{mass}$ and $[F_A]=\text{mass}^2$. Define the local three-form

$$K_3(A):=\operatorname{tr}\left(A\wedge dA+\frac23A\wedge A\wedge A\right)$$

and add the four-dimensional local counterterm $C_4=\lambda B\wedge K_3(A)$ to the effective action, with dimensionless coefficient $\lambda$. Under the $U(1)_V$ background transformation $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$ with $A$ fixed, its local variation is

$$\delta_\alpha C_4=\lambda\,d(\alpha K_3(A))-\lambda\,\alpha\operatorname{tr}(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The first term integrates to a boundary term and vanishes for compactly supported $\alpha$. Thus this counterterm shifts the $U(1)_V$ component of the local anomaly representative by $-\lambda\alpha\operatorname{tr}(F_A\wedge F_A)$ while the full relative class is unchanged modulo the admitted counterterm space. This calculation does not assert that the full $SU(3)\times U(1)_V$ anomaly vanishes or that the $SU(3)$ component of the representative is unchanged.

items.title: A conjugate SU(3)×U(1) chiral pair with zero local polynomial
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement:
Use the flat four-dimensional background data with global group $SU(3)\times U(1)_V$ and the common consistent regulator fixed above. Take the finite spectrum to consist of positive-chirality Weyl species $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$ and $E^*=(\bar{\mathbf3},-1)$. On a formal six-dimensional extension, write the anti-Hermitian $SU(3)$ curvature as $F_A$ and the $U(1)_V$ curvature as $f=dB$. The defining-representation curvature is $F_E=F_A+i f I_3$, with $\operatorname{tr}F_A=0$, so

$$\mathcal I_6(E)=\frac{i}{24\pi^2}\left(\operatorname{tr}F_A^3+3i f\wedge\operatorname{tr}F_A^2+3(if)^3\right).$$

The dual species has the opposite polynomial. The total polynomial and its common linear consistent descent therefore vanish, so this example has zero perturbative local anomaly class in the selected scheme. The six-dimensional extension is only the formal degree-six polynomial domain; the physical model remains four-dimensional.
